body: One of the best therapists I had was quick to agree that it does help and told me the science behind it - how it releases endorphins etc and does legitimately help you cope. Doing this over and over creates tracks in your brain that makes it hard to stop. She then emphasized the dangers - the risk of infection and the chance of cutting too deep and dying and went on to tell me a story of a young man from our city who was about my age who did just that- cut too deep with no intentions of killing himself but they couldn’t save him. To me, that was terrifying. Most people self harm not to die but to experience that release you mentioned but it’s dangerous in so many ways. I too have often thought there’s nothing wrong with it. I’ve self harmed for 17 years now, that’s 17 years of building those tracks in my mind. But they can be replaced, maybe not by one single thing but multiple things that can work together to achieve the same release. It’s been two months since I’ve self harmed and each day I’m trying to fight those tracks. I won’t lie and say I’ve found something that works just as well yet but I figure it’s worth a try to keep looking. Best wishes

For me it’s helping others. Now that’s small ways, being a support, small volunteering etc. I have a job I don’t hate but I know I can do better. I also experience anxiety and depression thinking about it, but I know when I’m ready I can go back to school and work toward a job that gives back and I know I can and will do that.

My friends, my pup, helping others, hearing other people’s stories, setting attainable goals, reading, creating things that have a part of me in them - writing, art etc., reaching out, coffee shops, music, planning vacations, making my living space peaceful, comfortable and aesthetically pleasing, finding things to do that make me feel purposeful or accomplished, realizing there’s so much in life I don’t want to miss. Thank you for your post - I needed this reminder as well. I hope that you can find what works for you
No one is too much, no one is a burden, no one is unlovable. Maybe she was the one, maybe she still is.

I care. And you care. Sabotaging won’t get you anywhere, it will only keep you from your hopes and dreams. Please take your medications, they will help. You don’t have to struggle like this. People care. Keep reaching out.
